close_reason: Landed in 5805464 alongside JMAP-t307.16. All three doc surfaces (example, src/lib.rs:7-33 rustdoc, README How-to-use) now use ? + Result. find_by_id().expect() replaced with if-let-Some + log-and-skip, which is what a real backend would write. Each surface adds a one-sentence preface naming RFC 8620 §3.6.2.
description:
Trigger: a consumer reads examples/parse_eml.rs (referenced from README §Examples) as a starting point for a real Email/get body materialisation path, copies the pattern verbatim into their backend, ships, and then receives hostile or malformed .eml input from a client (or a Sieve forward, or a federated peer).

Consequence: every .expect() in the example becomes a panic in a server context. parse(RAW).expect(...) panics on malformed MIME. find_by_id(...).expect('part must exist') panics if the part disappeared. decode_body_value(...).expect('decode failed') panics on charset trouble. A panicking JMAP server is a DoS surface — one crafted message kills the worker thread.

The workspace AGENTS.md rule 'No .unwrap() or .expect() in library code — propagate errors with ?' technically applies to library code only, so the example is not strictly violating the rule. But the example is the canonical 'how to use jmap-mime' artifact (README §Examples points at it), and consumers will copy from it. The lib.rs rustdoc example at src/lib.rs:7-33 has the same pattern, doubling the copy hazard.

Fix: rewrite examples/parse_eml.rs to:
- Return Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> from main and use ? throughout.
- For find_by_id, demonstrate the if-let-Some pattern (which is what a real backend writes anyway).
- Replace .expect('decode failed') with explicit match-on-Err that logs and skips, or returns the error.
- Add a comment near main() noting: 'A real backend MUST surface parse/decode errors as JMAP method errors, never panic.'

Same fix applies to src/lib.rs:7-33 rustdoc.

Belt-and-suspenders alternative: keep .expect() but add // SAFETY-IN-EXAMPLE-ONLY comments at each site explaining what a production caller does instead. Worse than the rewrite, because it leaves the panicking pattern visible.
title: examples/parse_eml.rs uses .expect() heavily; copy hazard for consumers
